title: "Set scores"

---

singscore (Foroutan et al. 2018) gives every run one score per gene set. Within a run, it ranks all
genes by abundance and averages the ranks of the set's members. A set whose members sit high in
that run scores high. The score depends only on ranks inside one run, so it does not move when
other runs are added or removed. This step computes scores and describes them; it tests nothing.

## Packages

singscore is called with `::` where used.

```{r}
#| label: packages
#| message: false
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "analysis_reporting_helpers.R"))
```

## Inputs

Ranking needs every protein in every run and cannot carry a covariate, so the input is limpa's
complete matrix with each protein's blood slope removed (`DAList_corrected.rds`). That matrix
inherits the blood-removal problem shown in `03_Quantification`: the 85 proteins measured in 20 or
fewer runs track blood more after removal, not less.

```{r}
#| label: inputs
out <- here("01_Processing", "05_Set_Scores", "c_data")
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
inputs <- c(
  gene_sets = "01_Processing/04_Gene_Sets/c_data/gene_sets.rds",
  proteins = "01_Processing/03_Quantification/c_data/DAList_corrected.rds"
)
paths <- map_chr(inputs, here)
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
gs <- readRDS(paths[["gene_sets"]])
proteins <- readRDS(paths[["proteins"]])
c(sets = length(gs$sets), proteins = nrow(proteins$data), runs = ncol(proteins$data))
```

Sets are keyed on gene symbols, so the matrix rows switch from accessions to the representative
gene chosen in `04_Gene_Sets`.

```{r}
#| label: gene-matrix
gene_map <- filter(gs$protein_map, selected)
stopifnot(
  identical(gene_map$uniprot_id, intersect(gene_map$uniprot_id, rownames(proteins$data))),
  !anyDuplicated(gene_map$gene)
)
gene_matrix <- as.matrix(proteins$data)[gene_map$uniprot_id, ]
rownames(gene_matrix) <- gene_map$gene
gene_matrix[1:3, 1:3]
```

## Scores

`rankGenes()` ranks genes within each run. `multiScore()` scores every set in one pass and also
returns each set's dispersion: the spread (median absolute deviation) of its members' ranks within
a run. Low dispersion means the members sit together; high means they scatter. By default singscore
centres the score so that 0 means the members' average rank equals the run's middle rank (package
behaviour).

```{r}
#| label: score
ranks <- singscore::rankGenes(gene_matrix)
scored <- singscore::multiScore(ranks, upSetColc = gs$sets)
scores <- scored$Scores
stopifnot(
  identical(rownames(scores), names(gs$sets)),
  identical(colnames(scores), colnames(proteins$data))
)
dim(scores)
round(scores[1:3, 1:4], 3)
```

Spread across sets within a run reflects which genes each set holds. Spread across runs within a
set is what the trait analyses use. Both are recorded.

```{r}
#| label: score-summary
score_summary <- tibble(
  n_sets = nrow(scores), n_samples = ncol(scores),
  min = round(min(scores), 4), max = round(max(scores), 4),
  mean = round(mean(scores), 4),
  mean_sd_across_sets = round(mean(apply(scores, 2, sd)), 4),
  mean_sd_across_samples = round(mean(apply(scores, 1, sd)), 4)
)
score_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: spread
set_spread <- gs$set_catalog |>
  filter(qualifies) |>
  transmute(set_id, collection) |>
  mutate(
    score = rowMeans(scores[set_id, ]),
    dispersion = rowMeans(scored$Dispersions[set_id, ])
  )
collection_spread <- set_spread |>
  summarise(
    n_sets = n(), median_score = round(median(score), 4),
    median_dispersion = round(median(dispersion), 1), .by = collection
  )
collection_spread
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-dispersion
#| fig-cap: "Each set's mean score against its mean dispersion, averaged over runs."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
ggplot(set_spread, aes(score, dispersion, colour = collection)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey80") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
  scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Dark2", name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3, alpha = 1))) +
  labs(x = "mean score across runs", y = "mean dispersion across runs") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Every set's score in every run, pooled within each group-by-time cell."
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4
tibble(
  group = rep(proteins$metadata$group[match(colnames(scores), proteins$metadata$sample_id)],
    each = nrow(scores)
  ),
  score = as.vector(scores)
) |>
  ggplot(aes(score, group)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.12, outlier.shape = NA, linewidth = 0.3) +
  labs(x = "singscore", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)
```

## How much of the score variation is the person

A PCA of the score matrix, then a one-way ANOVA of PC1 and PC2 on the person (`subject`). The
subject share is the fraction of each component's variance that person identity explains. A large
share is why the trait step analyses within-person change beside the baseline level.

```{r}
#| label: structure
components <- prcomp(t(scores), scale. = FALSE)
variance <- summary(components)$importance[2, 1:4]
targets <- proteins$metadata[match(rownames(components$x), proteins$metadata$sample_id), ]
participant_share <- map_dbl(1:2, function(i) {
  terms <- summary(aov(components$x[, i] ~ targets$subject))[[1]]
  terms[1, 2] / sum(terms[, 2])
})
structure_check <- tibble(
  component = paste0("PC", 1:4),
  variance_explained = round(as.numeric(variance), 3),
  subject_share = c(round(participant_share, 3), NA, NA)
)
structure_check
```

## Summary

`r nrow(scores)` sets were scored in `r ncol(scores)` runs. Scores range from
`r round(min(scores), 2)` to `r round(max(scores), 2)`. Person identity explains
`r round(100 * participant_share[1])`% of PC1 and `r round(100 * participant_share[2])`% of PC2.

## Save

`singscore.rds` is read by the set contrasts, classification and trait steps.

```{r}
#| label: save
saveRDS(list(scores = scores), file.path(out, "singscore.rds"), compress = "xz")
sheets <- list(
  score_summary = score_summary,
  collection_spread = collection_spread,
  set_spread = set_spread,
  structure_check = structure_check,
  set_scores = rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(scores), "set_id")
)
holds <- c(
  "Range and spread of the score matrix.",
  "Median score and dispersion per collection.",
  "Mean score and dispersion per set across samples.",
  "Variance explained by the first four components, and the subject share of PC1 and PC2.",
  "The set by sample score matrix, as saved in singscore.rds."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "set_scores.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
```
